Package org.apache.juneau.bean.mcp.v20260728

Class ElicitSchema

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.bean.mcp.v20260728.ElicitSchema
public class ElicitSchema extends Object
Fluent builder for a restricted elicitation JSON Schema (MCP 2026-07-28 SEP-2322), producing the JsonMap consumed by ElicitRequest.setRequestedSchema(java.util.Map).

The elicitation restricted schema permits only primitive-typed, non-nested top-level properties. There is deliberately no objectField/arrayField method, so a nested/object/array-typed field is a compile-time impossibility, never a runtime-rejected one. build() additionally rejects a handful of structurally-invalid per-field modifier combinations (for example format(String) on a non-string field) with an IllegalStateException, so a handler author gets an immediate, in-process failure rather than a wire-level schema-validation error discovered by the client much later.

Each xxxField(name) call starts a new field and becomes the target of every subsequent modifier call (title(String), description(String), etc.) until the next xxxField(...) call. Re-declaring a field under a name already used by an earlier xxxField(...) call replaces that field's definition entirely, silently discarding any per-field modifiers already applied to it (last-field-wins). minLength(int)/maxLength(int) are additional string-only per-field modifiers, alongside format(String). required(String...) is a separate, builder-level (not per-field) call that marks one or more field names required, emitting a top-level "required":[...] array; unlike the per-field modifiers, it is not tied to the most-recently-started field, is order-independent with respect to xxxField(...) (a name may be marked required before or after the field it names is (re)declared, and a redeclaration of that field does not discard the marking), and may be called any time, with an unknown name validated only at build() time.

Example:

JsonMap schema = ElicitSchema.create() .booleanField("confirm").title("Confirm") .build();

    • required

      public ElicitSchema required(String... names)
      Marks one or more already-added field names required, contributing to the built schema's top-level "required":[...] array.

      Unlike the per-field modifiers (title(String), etc.), this is a builder-level, not per-field, call — it is not tied to the most-recently-started field and may name any field(s) already added via an earlier xxxField(...) call, in any order. May be called more than once; each call adds to the previously-marked names (not replaced). Naming a field not (yet) added is rejected at build() time, not here, since a later xxxField(...) call may still add it.

      Parameters:
      names - The field names to mark required. Must not be null or empty, and must not contain a null element.
      Returns:
      This object (for method chaining).
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If names is null, empty, or contains a null element.

    • build

      public JsonMap build()
      Validates every field's modifier combination (and the builder-level required(String...) marking) and builds the final restricted-schema JsonMap ({"type":"object","properties":{...},"required":[...]}, the last member present only if required(String...) was called at least once).
      Returns:
      The built schema, ready for ElicitRequest.setRequestedSchema(java.util.Map).
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - If no field was ever added, if any field carries a structurally-invalid modifier combination, or if required(String...) named a field that was never added.
